name: The used RTX 3090 is no longer ~$550-650 - street price is ~$900-1,000 and moved +27% in one quarter
symptom: Any cost model or buying decision predicated on a ~$550-650 used 3090 is now wrong by ~40-60%. The current realistic per-card band is ~$900-1,000.
root_cause: Used-market repricing: Hardware Corner's tracker measured used 3090s at $750 Nov-2025 rising to ~$950 by Feb-2026 (+27% in 3 months), and their page now lists ~$1,000 avg market value. Demand for cheap 24GB CUDA cards outstripped the used supply.
workaround: Budget ~$850-1,000/card used, or catch auction dips. Re-verify eBay completed sales (not just asks) at purchase time - this figure is volatile. Re-run multi-GPU math at the new price: a 4x 3090 rig is now ~$4.5-4.8K all-in for 96GB, still under one RTX PRO 6000's $8,800 but no longer the steal it was at $650/card.
notes: The value edge eroded but nothing else at 24GB undercuts the 3090 on speed+stack maturity. Buy only if found <=$800; otherwise the gap to 32GB cards (used 4090, RTX PRO, or 4x B70 for capacity) is small enough to matter. A 3090 Ti (~+9% TG) trades at the same price.
